title: High-Throughput Distributed Tracing & APM Platform in Go with ClickHouse Columnar Storage & Grafana Flamegraphs
problem: Commercial Application Performance Monitoring (APM) SaaS platforms charge exorbitant rates for high-volume distributed trace ingestion, forcing engineering teams to drop trace fidelity or pay unpredictable bills. Ingesting millions of OpenTelemetry spans into relational or document databases causes severe disk write saturation and sluggish multi-hop trace retrieval queries. This project builds a production-grade distributed tracing and APM platform in Go and ClickHouse. The system ingests OpenTelemetry (OTLP) traces over gRPC and HTTP, stores span hierarchies in optimized ClickHouse columnar tables, implements tail-based sampling to retain error traces while filtering routine telemetry, and exposes query APIs powering interactive trace flamegraphs in Grafana.

use_cases.title: Microservice Distributed Bottleneck Diagnosis
use_cases.first_sentence: Platform engineering teams maintaining hundreds of microservices need to pinpoint the exact downstream RPC service causing latency spikes in user-facing checkout flows.
use_cases.second_sentence: The platform aggregates distributed trace spans across services, rendering end-to-end waterfall flamegraphs in Grafana that highlight slow database queries and queuing delays.

use_cases.title: Automated Error Trace Retention & Anomaly Filtering
use_cases.first_sentence: Site reliability engineers require 100% capture of failed transactions and exceptions without drowning in gigabytes of mundane health check telemetry.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine applies tail-based sampling rules, retaining all spans associated with HTTP 5xx errors or exceptions while sampling down healthy traces to sustainable storage volumes.

use_cases.title: SLA & SLO Service Latency Percentile Compliance Auditing
use_cases.first_sentence: Cloud infrastructure architects must audit third-party API service level agreements by calculating p95 and p99 latency percentiles across millions of daily API transactions.
use_cases.second_sentence: The ClickHouse columnar engine executes analytical aggregation queries across billions of spans in milliseconds, generating real-time SLO latency compliance reports.

hard_parts: Designing high-throughput ClickHouse columnar table schemas with optimal sorting keys (ServiceName, StartTime, TraceId) for sub-second span queries
Implementing tail-based sampling buffers in Go that hold trace spans in memory until trace completion before deciding retention
Streaming OTLP binary protobuf payloads over gRPC with high-concurrency worker pools and batched database inserts
Constructing parent-child tree reconstruction algorithms that assemble distributed span waterfall graphs from out-of-order span chunks
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase cleanly separating OTLP ingestion receivers, tail-based sampling buffers, and ClickHouse repository layers
High-throughput benchmark report validating 25,000+ spans per second sustained ingestion into ClickHouse with sub-45ms trace retrieval
Anti-fake verification script emitting a synthetic distributed trace with a novel span attribute and asserting the complete tree is reconstructible via API

architecture.data_flow: Microservices emit OTLP trace spans over gRPC to the Go receiver; the receiver pushes spans into the tail-based sampling engine; the sampling engine buffers spans for a temporal window (e.g. 5 seconds) to observe the complete trace lifecycle; if any span in the trace contains an error status or latency exceeding thresholds, the entire trace is marked for retention; accepted traces flush in batches of 5,000 spans to ClickHouse; the trace query API queries ClickHouse by TraceID, sorts spans by timestamp, resolves parent-child relationships, and serves the waterfall flamegraph payload to Grafana.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: ClickHouse primary keys on (ServiceName, toStartOfHour(StartTime), TraceId) ensuring fast scan pruning; bounded buffer sizes preventing memory leaks.

riskiest_component.name: ClickHouse Write Amplification from Too-Frequent Small Batch Inserts
riskiest_component.mitigation: Buffer incoming spans in Go memory and flush in atomic batches of 5,000 to 10,000 rows or every 1 second.
riskiest_component.fallback: ClickHouse asynchronous inserts feature (async_insert=1) with in-database buffering.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a distributed tracing storage and APM engine in Go with ClickHouse columnar tables, tail-based sampling, and Grafana flamegraphs.
worksheet.q2: Target users: observability platform engineers, infrastructure architects, and SRE specialists.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: microservice bottleneck diagnosis, automated error trace retention, and SLA/SLO latency compliance auditing.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: ClickHouse table schema indexing for span lookups, tail-based sampling buffering without memory exhaustion, gRPC OTLP batching, and span parent-child reconstruction.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: OpenTelemetry collector configs, ClickHouse DDL schemas, and synthetic trace generators. Synthetic telemetry only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local SQLite or in-memory columnar slice store.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: ClickHouse write amplification from small batches. Fallback: Go memory buffering and atomic 5,000-row flushes.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mock hardcoded trace arrays. Anti-fake check 5 emits dynamic trace with unique attribute and error status, asserts ClickHouse query returns exact DAG.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local loopback Docker containers and synthetic telemetry only, zero production infrastructure exposure.
